reasons: Includes tests that prove the fingerprint and body checks can fail.
Failure messages give the exact command to fix the problem.
Does not run the TypeScript compiler, so compile errors are caught elsewhere.

terms.meaning: a short code computed from a file's contents that changes when the contents change
a fixed-length code computed from data, used to detect changes
a specific, widely used hash method
a written description of the allowed shape of a record
a file produced by a program rather than typed by people
a TypeScript description of the fields an object must have
a Python library that defines data shapes as classes and checks data against them
the runtime needed to run JavaScript and frontend build tools

used_by: Run by pytest; no other file imports it

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and the three guard layers
sections.what: Explains that the schema is exported, turned into TypeScript types by a generator, and that this file checks the final step. Sets the paths to the schema, the generated types, and the generator.
sections.why: The header explains that only the last layer had no guard.
sections.watch_out: These paths must match the real file locations. Moving any of them breaks every test in this file.

sections.name: fingerprint
sections.title: Short hash function
sections.what: Computes a 16-character code from a set of bytes using SHA-256, shortened.
sections.why: One hashing rule is used everywhere, so the stamped value and the computed value always match in form.
sections.watch_out: Changing the length or the method breaks the match with every stamped header.

sections.name: schema_fingerprint
sections.title: Fingerprint of the schema file
sections.what: Computes the fingerprint of the schema file's exact bytes, so any change counts, including a reworded description.
sections.why: The docstring says byte-level matching is deliberate, because a reworded description changes the doc comments in the generated file.
sections.watch_out: Changes to whitespace or line endings change the fingerprint even when the meaning is the same.

sections.name: body_of
sections.title: Removing the header from the generated file
sections.what: Returns everything after the generator's standard marker line, which is the part whose hash is checked for hand-edits.
sections.why: Likely reason: so the header stamp itself is not part of the body that is hashed.
sections.watch_out: If the generator changes its marker line, this cuts the wrong part and the body check fails.

sections.name: TestTheGeneratedTypesExist
sections.title: Checks that the generated files exist and are marked
sections.what: Confirms the schema, the generator, and the generated types file are present, and that the types file header says it is generated and names the schema.
sections.why: A file a reader might edit by hand is one that will be edited by hand, so the warning text is checked.
sections.watch_out: Rewording the warning text in the generator breaks this check.

sections.name: TestTheHandWrittenMirrorMatchesTheGeneratedType (part 1)
sections.title: Matching the hand-written confidence copy to the generated type
sections.what: Reads which fields are optional in the viewer's hand-written confidence block and in the generated type, and fails if any field differs in optionality or if the sets of fields differ. The docstring records a past case where a required field was made optional in the copy, so the viewer accepted records the schema refuses.
sections.why: A hand-written copy does not update when the schema changes, so its optional and required fields are compared with the generated type.
sections.watch_out: Only optionality and field names are compared, so a type mismatch in the copy is not caught here.

sections.name: TestTheHandWrittenMirrorMatchesTheGeneratedType: test_the_mirror_has_no_default_for_a_required_field
sections.title: No fallback default for a required field
sections.what: Checks that the viewer source does not contain the old default list or the fallback expression for the contributing features field.
sections.why: A default in the viewer would invent a value nobody computed.
sections.watch_out: This is a text match, so a renamed default or a different fallback style would pass unnoticed.

sections.name: TestTheTypesAreNotStale (part 1)
sections.title: Staleness and hand-edit checks
sections.what: Confirms the stamped fingerprint matches the current schema, the stamped schema id matches the schema's id, and the stamped body hash matches the generated file's body. Also includes a test that shows the hand-edit check can fail.
sections.why: The schema fingerprint cannot see a hand-edit to the generated file, so a separate body hash is needed.
sections.watch_out: Any manual edit to the generated file, even a comment, fails the body check. The fix is to regenerate, not to adjust the hash.

sections.name: TestTheTypesAreNotStale: test_the_schema_fingerprint_moves_with_the_schema
sections.title: The schema fingerprint responds to changes
sections.what: Changes the schema title in a temporary copy and confirms the fingerprint changes.
sections.why: Confirms the fingerprint function really responds to the schema rather than matching by accident.
sections.watch_out: Relies on the title text appearing once in the schema, so changing that wording may affect this test.

sections.name: TestTheTypesDescribeTheWholeContract
sections.title: Generated types cover the whole contract
sections.what: Confirms the generated file has an interface for each top-level block of the record. Also confirms that two scoring dimensions, fragmentation and change burden, keep their note that a score of five means worse.
sections.why: A generator that produced a partial file could still pass the hash check, so completeness is checked separately.
sections.watch_out: The inversion check looks at a fixed window of characters before each field, so moving the note far from its field makes the check fail.

summary: Checks that the generated TypeScript types for the process record were produced from the current schema, have not been hand-edited, and still describe the whole contract.
purpose: Stop the frontend types from quietly falling out of step with the Python schema.
why: The header explains three layers of protection, and that only the last layer, the generated TypeScript file, had no guard. A generated file is only as current as its last regeneration, so this file stamps and checks a fingerprint.
how: Computes a short hash of the schema file and compares it with the hash stamped in the generated file's header. Computes a second hash of the file body to detect hand-edits. Checks the schema id, that the file is marked as generated, that each top-level block has an interface, and that two scoring dimensions keep their inversion note.
inputs: The schema JSON file, the generated TypeScript file, and the generator script, all read from the repository.
outputs: Pytest pass or fail, with messages telling the developer to regenerate the types.
risks: If the generator changes its output format, the header patterns may stop matching and checks may fail even when nothing is wrong. The documentation check reads a fixed window of characters before a field, which is fragile. The file runs without Node, so it cannot confirm the TypeScript compiles.
debug: If the fingerprint check fails, the schema changed without regeneration, so run the generate command in the frontend folder. If the body check fails, someone edited the generated file, so revert that edit and change the schema or generator instead. If the documentation check fails, look at the comment text near the named field in the generated file.
